AgentChatRequest-Input.description:
Request body for the unified agent chat endpoint.

Parameters
----------
message : str
    The user's message to the agent.  Required, non-empty.
document_id : str
    MongoDB ObjectId of the document being discussed.  Required,
    non-empty.
chat_id : str or None
    Existing chat UUID to resume a conversation.  ``None`` starts
    a new conversation.
leaf_id : int or None
    The message whose branch the run continues: its chain from the root
    is the history, and the new message is its child. ``None`` continues
    from the chat's newest message.
model : str or None
    The CLI model for the ``claude`` / ``codex`` engines: a model id or
    alias the CLI understands (e.g. ``sonnet``). ``None`` uses the CLI's
    own default. The ``gateway`` engine refuses it; its models are chosen
    by ``gateway_models``.
engine : {"gateway", "claude", "codex"}
    Which backend runs the agent loop. ``gateway`` (the default) is Magic
    LLM over the configured gateway. ``claude`` and ``codex`` run the
    developer's own Claude Code / Codex CLI under their own account
    login; they exist only when ``COLWRITE_ENVIRONMENT=local`` and the
    request comes directly from the same machine, and are rejected with an
    ``ENGINE_*`` SSE error otherwise.
gateway_models : GatewayModelSelection or None
    First choices for gateway main/lite work, limited to the chains exposed
    by GET /api/agent/engines. Applies to helper calls under every engine.
    ``main`` also selects the gateway loop's model; CLI loop models are
    chosen by ``model``.
mode : {"assistant", "rewrite"}
    Which tools the agent is given.  ``assistant`` (the default) is the
    chat panel: the agent can read, edit and create documents.
    ``rewrite`` is the selection toolbar, where the *client* owns applying
    the result through its accept/reject affordance — handing that agent
    ``doc_edit`` made it mutate the stored document behind the user's back
    while the toolbar was still offering them the choice.
apply_mode : {"propose", "auto"}
    Both store the same atomic change sets; ``doc_edit`` never moves the
    page head. ``propose`` (the default) leaves every set for the author
    to review. ``auto`` asks for the sets to be applied by the open
    editor without review (D18). The server grants it only in
    ``assistant`` mode, for an editor or above, under a workspace policy
    that allows it, and with no web-research tool enabled; each set then
    carries ``apply_policy: "auto"``, otherwise ``"review"`` with an
    ``auto_blocked_reason``. The run's ``status`` events report the
    effective policy. ``auto`` is refused in ``rewrite`` mode.
ephemeral : bool
    Run without creating or extending a chat. For the editor's inline
    AI (a rewrite of a selection, a drafted paragraph): those requests are
    one-shot, and persisting each one as a conversation filled the chat
    list with single-message chats. The run itself — usage, duration, tool
    executions — is still recorded. Only valid in ``rewrite`` mode and
    without ``chat_id``.
context : AgentContext or None
    Where the author is working: the caret's block, selected text, and
    blocks referenced in the message. Only blocks the model can see are
    kept.

chat_id.title: Chat Id

context.description: The author's caret block, selection and referenced blocks; blocks the model cannot see are ignored.

AgentContext.description:
Where the author is working, sent alongside the message.

Words like "this paragraph", "here" or "the selection" mean something
only relative to the editor. Pasting that into the message made it part
of what the author said; carried here it is context the server checks
against the visible document (unknown and ``aiHidden`` blocks are
dropped) and shows the model under its own heading.

block_id.description: The block the author's caret was in.
block_id.title: Block Id

block_ids.description: Blocks the author referenced in the message.
block_ids.title: Block Ids

selection.description: Text the author had selected, if any.

AgentContext.title: AgentContext

AgentPaperSourceOption.description: One selectable paper-search provider and its effective state.
AgentPaperSourceOption.title: AgentPaperSourceOption

AgentSelection.description: Text the author had selected in one block when they sent the message.
AgentSelection.title: AgentSelection

AgentToolCategory.description: A stable display group for related agent tools.
AgentToolCategory.title: AgentToolCategory

AgentToolOption.title: AgentToolOption

AgentToolSettingsResponse.title: AgentToolSettingsResponse

A signed-in session as the browser sees it: no credential, ever.

The access and refresh tokens travel only as HttpOnly cookies.
AuthSessionResponse.title: AuthSessionResponse

file.description: A PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF image.
file.title: File

location.description: Where the PDF goes. There is no default.
location.title: Location

ChangeSetDecisionsRequest.description:
The author's decision on one or more operations of a change set.

Operations are addressed by their index in ``operations``. Several can be
decided in one request, because rejecting an operation can take the ones
built on it along and the reviewer decides those together.
ChangeSetDecisionsRequest.title: ChangeSetDecisionsRequest

ChangeSetOperationTargetResponse.description:
The existing block an operation rewrites or deletes.

``fingerprint`` is the block as the batch found it, and
``head_fingerprint`` the same digest for that block in the head this
response was read at (``compared_head_seq``); it is ``null`` when the
block is no longer in the document or the response was not compared with
a head. The two differ when the saved block changed after the proposal.
ChangeSetOperationTargetResponse.title: ChangeSetOperationTargetResponse

ChatMessageChain.description: The chain from the chat's first message to the leaf, root first.
ChatMessageChain.title: ChatMessageChain

CheckAvailabilityRequest.description: Check one or both server-supported registration identifiers.
CheckAvailabilityRequest.title: CheckAvailabilityRequest

CitationSource.description: Frontend citation metadata retained without lossy projection.
CitationSource.title: CitationSource

ClaimAssessment.description: Source-backed claim verdict returned by the public tool and route.

disclaimer.default: This assessment is limited to the retrieved excerpts and is not a substitute for reading the papers or expert review.
disclaimer.title: Disclaimer

ClaimAssessment.title: ClaimAssessment

ClaimEvidenceFinding.description: One selected excerpt plus its source metadata.
ClaimEvidenceFinding.title: ClaimEvidenceFinding

CodeBlock.description:
Preformatted text — source code, pseudocode, program output.

``text`` is plain text, never html: whitespace is significant and nothing
in it is markup, so it bypasses the inline-html sanitizer entirely.
CodeBlock.title: CodeBlock

CollectionDetail.description: One collection, its breadcrumb, its subtree counts and its ETag.
CollectionDetail.title: CollectionDetail

CollectionGrantState.description:
Whether one page can use a collection's PDFs, and through which grant.

``direct`` is a grant on this collection itself. ``effective`` is true
when this collection or one above it is granted; ``via_collection_id`` and
``via_collection_name`` name the nearest granted one.
CollectionGrantState.title: CollectionGrantState

CollectionPathItem.description: One collection of a root-to-collection path.
CollectionPathItem.title: CollectionPathItem

CollectionRestoreResult.description:
The collection is back, at its place or at the top level when that
place is gone (``moved_to_root``). ``job`` brings its pages back; the
answer is 202 while it has pages to bring back.
CollectionRestoreResult.title: CollectionRestoreResult

CollectionSummary.description: One child in a collection listing, with its counts and its ETag.
CollectionSummary.title: CollectionSummary

CollectionTrashPreview.description:
What moving the collection to the Trash takes with it: its active
subtree, the pages homed there and the PDFs located there. Send the
counts back as the trash request's ``expected_*``.
CollectionTrashPreview.title: CollectionTrashPreview

CollectionTrashRequest.description:
The preview the author confirmed. Any drift is 409
``preview_changed`` and nothing moves.
CollectionTrashRequest.title: CollectionTrashRequest

CollectionTrashResult.description:
The collection is a trash root now. ``job`` moves its pages to the
Trash; the answer is 202 while it has pages to move.
CollectionTrashResult.title: CollectionTrashResult

CollectionUpdateRequest.description: Only the fields present change. ``description: null`` clears it.
CollectionUpdateRequest.title: CollectionUpdateRequest

DeletedWorkspaceSummary.description: A deleted workspace its owner can restore until ``purge_after``.
DeletedWorkspaceSummary.title: DeletedWorkspaceSummary

DocumentActivityResponse.description: What happened on one page, from the activity the API records.
DocumentActivityResponse.title: DocumentActivityResponse

DocumentContent-Input.description: Complete canonical semantic content for schema version 1.
DocumentContent-Input.title: DocumentContent

DocumentContent-Output.description: Complete canonical semantic content for schema version 1.
DocumentContent-Output.title: DocumentContent

DocumentCreateRequest.description:
A new page: its content, and where it goes.

``collection_id`` ``null`` (the default) is the workspace's top level.
``position`` places it among that home's pages: ``"last"`` (the
default), ``{after_id}`` or ``{before_id}`` naming a page there.
DocumentCreateRequest.title: DocumentCreateRequest

DocumentListResponse.description:
One page of a list; ``next_cursor`` continues it. Lists carry no
totals: counts come from the workspace read.
DocumentListResponse.title: DocumentListResponse

DocumentLocationResponse.description: Where a page lives. ``collection_id`` is ``null`` for the root.
DocumentLocationResponse.title: DocumentLocationResponse

DocumentMoveRequest.description: A new home for a page: a collection, or ``null`` for the root.
DocumentMoveRequest.title: DocumentMoveRequest

DocumentPlacementResponse.description:
Where a page lives after a move or reorder.

``placement_etag`` (``"cwp:{placement_seq}"``) is the If-Match of the
next move. The content ETag did not change.
DocumentPlacementResponse.title: DocumentPlacementResponse

DocumentReorderRequest.description: A new place among the page's current siblings.
DocumentReorderRequest.title: DocumentReorderRequest

DocumentStateResponse.description:
Working state of a document plus its position in the version tree.

``revision_id``/``revision_no`` describe the newest committed revision,
while ``current_revision_id`` is the tree node the working content sits
on. They differ only after a restore, which moves the current pointer to
an existing revision without committing a new one; the next save commits a
revision parented on that node and forks the tree.
DocumentStateResponse.title: DocumentStateResponse

DocumentSummaryResponse.description:
One page in a list. It carries no concurrency token: the ETag comes
from the page read.
DocumentSummaryResponse.title: DocumentSummaryResponse

DoneEventMessage.description: A stored ``done`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
DoneEventMessage.title: DoneEventMessage

EmailAddress.description:
One of a user's email addresses (owner view).

Mirrors the provider's owner email row. The provider never returns the raw
address in list payloads — only ``email_masked`` and the normalized ``email``
may be present — so consumers should display ``email_masked`` when available.
EmailAddress.title: EmailAddress

EngineStatusResponse.description: One engine and whether this request may run it.
EngineStatusResponse.title: EngineStatusResponse

ErrorEventMessage.description: A stored ``error`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
ErrorEventMessage.title: ErrorEventMessage

FieldError.description: One request-validation failure, addressed by its location.
FieldError.title: FieldError

GatewayModelSelection.description: First choices from the server's main and lite model chains.
GatewayModelSelection.title: GatewayModelSelection

GatewayModels.description: The configured gateway model chain per tier.
GatewayModels.title: GatewayModels

Invitation.description: A pending invitation, as its workspace's admins see it.
Invitation.title: Invitation

InvitationAcceptance.description:
The caller is a member of ``workspace_id`` with ``role``.
``already_member``: they were before, and kept their role.
InvitationAcceptance.title: InvitationAcceptance

InvitationCreateRequest.description:
Invite an address. The address is used for its hash and a masked hint,
and is not stored.
InvitationCreateRequest.title: InvitationCreateRequest

InvitationCreated.description:
The invitation and its token. The token is the secret part of the link
the inviter shares (the API sends no email): give it to
``POST /invitations/accept``. A replay of the request with the same
``Idempotency-Key`` answers the same token; no other read ever does.
InvitationCreated.title: InvitationCreated

InvitationListResponse.description:
The pending invitations, newest first. ``next_cursor`` is always
``null``.
InvitationListResponse.title: InvitationListResponse

JobProgress.description:
How far a job is. ``dry_run`` is set when the purge is in its dry
run, with the first ``items`` it would have deleted. ``result`` is set
when a copy or an export is done.
JobProgress.title: JobProgress

JobResult.description:
What a finished copy or export made.

A copy names the new page (``document_id``) in the job's workspace and
how many PDFs it copied. An export counts the pages and PDFs in the zip,
its size, and when it stops being downloadable.
JobResult.title: JobResult

MemberListResponse.description:
Every active member: owners first, then admins, editors and viewers,
each by name. The whole list in one answer; ``next_cursor`` is always
``null``.
MemberListResponse.title: MemberListResponse

MessageImage.description: A chat image attached to a user message.
MessageImage.title: MessageImage

MessagePdf.description: One of the workspace's PDFs attached to a user message.
MessagePdf.title: MessagePdf

OpenAccessLocation.description: Public full-text location and its upstream licensing information.
OpenAccessLocation.title: OpenAccessLocation

OwnershipTransferModel.description:
A pending transfer of the workspace's ownership. Nothing changes until
``to_user_id`` accepts; then they are the owner and ``from_user_id`` an
admin. It lapses at ``expire_time``.
OwnershipTransferModel.title: OwnershipTransferModel

PageActivity.description: One recently edited page and its activity in the workspace.
PageActivity.title: PageActivity

PageCopyAccepted.description:
202: the copy runs as ``job`` in the target workspace. Poll it with
``GET /workspaces/{target_workspace_id}/jobs/{job.id}``; when it is done,
``job.progress.result.document_id`` is the new page there.
PageCopyAccepted.title: PageCopyAccepted

PageCopyRequest.description:
Copy a page into another workspace.

The copy gets the page's content (blocks, sources, citation style, name,
tags). ``include_pdfs`` adds the PDFs located on the page (``located``)
and those in the collections it uses (``located_and_granted``); each
becomes a PDF of the target workspace located on the copy, reusing the
extraction. History, review, chats and PDF grants are never copied.
PageCopyRequest.title: PageCopyRequest

PaperPayload.description: A paper as the research routes return it.
PaperPayload.title: PaperPayload

PdfGrant.description:
A collection a page uses, with its path.

``origin`` is ``manual`` for a grant the author added, ``setting`` for
one the collection's "Pages here can use these PDFs" added; that one is
removed when the page leaves the collection.
PdfGrant.title: PdfGrant

PdfGrantState.description: A page's grant state for one collection after a grant change.
PdfGrantState.title: PdfGrantState

ProblemDetails.description:
An ``application/problem+json`` body.

The members after ``retryable`` are extensions; the registry says which
ones a given ``code`` may carry, and absent ones are omitted.
ProblemDetails.title: ProblemDetails

ProviderProvenance.description: One upstream observation of a normalized research object.
ProviderProvenance.title: ProviderProvenance

ReasoningEventMessage.description: A stored ``reasoning`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
ReasoningEventMessage.title: ReasoningEventMessage

RegisterRequest.description: Consumer signup; email identities are verified after registration.
RegisterRequest.title: RegisterRequest

ResearchEvidence.description: A source-backed excerpt usable by a downstream claim assessor.
ResearchEvidence.title: ResearchEvidence

ResourceItem.description: One PDF of the workspace: where it is, and its extraction.
ResourceItem.title: ResourceItem

ResourceMarkdownWindow.description: One window of a PDF's extracted Markdown.
ResourceMarkdownWindow.title: ResourceMarkdownWindow

ResourceSearchSkipped.description: A PDF the search could not read yet, and why.
ResourceSearchSkipped.title: ResourceSearchSkipped

RevisionMetadataResponse.description:
One node of the version tree.

``revision_no`` is a global creation ordinal; ``parent_revision_id`` is the
only lineage statement, so siblings sharing a parent are branches created
by saving after a restore. A restore writes no revision of its own.
RevisionMetadataResponse.title: RevisionMetadataResponse

RevisionRestoreRequest.description:
Options for moving the document onto an existing revision.

``summary`` annotates the restore audit event; a restore commits no
revision, so the summary never becomes revision metadata.
RevisionRestoreRequest.title: RevisionRestoreRequest

RunStatusEventMessage.description: A stored ``run.status`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
RunStatusEventMessage.title: RunStatusEventMessage

RunsCancelReply.description:
The run after the cancel: ``cancelled`` when it was still queued,
``cancelling`` while it stops, or its terminal status when it had already
finished.
RunsCancelReply.title: RunsCancelReply

RunsStartReply.description: The admitted run; a replayed ``request_id`` returns the stored run.
RunsStartReply.title: RunsStartReply

SessionChatEventMessage.description: A stored ``session.chat`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
SessionChatEventMessage.title: SessionChatEventMessage

SessionPlan.description:
Subscription-only plan projection embedded in identity/session responses.

Mirrors ``api.auth`` ``SessionPlanStatus``. ``state`` is one of
none|free|trial|active|past_due|canceled for the session's project (resolved through
its billing group). Subscriptions only; packages/credits are consumer-owned.
SessionPlan.title: SessionPlan

SourceEntry.description: One source a research tool returned; shaped like a ``CitationSource``.
SourceEntry.title: SourceEntry

SourcesEventMessage.description: A stored ``sources`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
SourcesEventMessage.title: SourcesEventMessage

StatusEventMessage.description: A stored ``status`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
StatusEventMessage.title: StatusEventMessage

SubagentEventMessage.description: A stored ``subagent`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
SubagentEventMessage.title: SubagentEventMessage

TodoEventMessage.description: A stored ``todo`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
TodoEventMessage.title: TodoEventMessage

TokenEventMessage.description: A stored ``token`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
TokenEventMessage.title: TokenEventMessage

ToolActionEventMessage.description: A stored ``tool_action`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
ToolActionEventMessage.title: ToolActionEventMessage

ToolCallArgsEventMessage.description: A stored ``tool_call_args`` event, as a subscription delivers it.
ToolCallArgsEventMessage.title: ToolCallArgsEventMessage

A registry `ErrorCode` when the tool refused the call (`workspace_policy`, `no_workspace_context`, `no_document_context`, `document_validation_failed`, …); otherwise the failure type the tool runtime reports (`TimeoutError`, `ContentTruncated`, `MalformedArgumentsError`, `UnknownToolError`, `RepeatedToolFailure`, …, or the class name of an exception the tool raised).

TrashCounts.description:
What a collection trash root holds. Deleting it forever takes these
as its ``expected_*`` counts.

One trash root. ``id`` is a collection or PDF id as a string, or a

Partial profile update.

Only the fields present in the request body are changed; an explicit
empty string clears a field.  Username, email, and password belong to the
auth service and are deliberately absent here — ``extra="forbid"``
rejects them rather than quietly ignoring them.

UserProfileModel.description: The profile ColWrite owns, independent of the auth service.

The workspace is deleted for every member. Its owner can restore it
until ``purge_after``; then it is purged from every store.

WorkspaceDetailResponse.description: One workspace, with its counts and its ETag (``"cww:{row_version}"``).
WorkspaceDetailResponse.title: WorkspaceDetailResponse

Work that finishes after the request answered. Poll it with
``GET /workspaces/{workspace_id}/jobs/{job_id}`` until ``done`` or

The personal workspace is always present. ``last_workspace_id`` is the

WorkspacePolicyModel.description:
What the assistant may do in this workspace, on top of each person's
own tool settings. ``false`` turns a feature off for everyone here; it
never turns on what a person turned off.

- ``outside_research``: outside research providers (paper indexes, the
  claim assessor) and the identifier lookups of citing;
- ``auto``: Auto mode; refused runs report ``auto_blocked_reason:

get.description:
Find the workspace of a page from a bare link.

A member of the page's workspace gets ``{workspace_id, collection_id}``
and opens the page under that workspace. Anyone else gets 404
``document_not_found``, the same answer as for a page that does not
exist.

post.description:
Join the workspace an invitation names, with its role.

The invited address must be one of the caller's verified addresses at the
auth service (``GET /auth/emails``): otherwise 403
``invitation_email_mismatch``. An unknown, revoked or used token, or one
whose workspace is gone, is 404 ``invitation_not_found``; a lapsed one is
410 ``invitation_expired``. Accepting again as the member it added
answers ``already_member``; a member already there keeps their role.

get.description: Search the first 1,000 relevance-ranked Semantic Scholar results.

Resolve a DOI, arXiv id or Semantic Scholar id.

Returns ``{"source": {...}}`` shaped like a document ``CitationSource``.

- 400 ``unrecognized_identifier``: not a DOI, arXiv or S2 identifier.
- 403 ``paper_source_disabled``: an S2 id while Semantic Scholar is off.
- 404 ``source_not_found``: the registry does not know it.
- 503 ``resolver_unavailable``: the registry could not be reached — the
  identifier may be valid; try again.

delete.description:
Delete the account and everything it alone owns, and end the session.

It is refused with 409 ``sole_owner`` (``workspace_ids``) while a live
shared workspace has the caller as its only owner: delete it first. A
username that does not match is 409 ``confirmation_mismatch``. Otherwise
the personal workspace, and every deleted shared workspace the caller
solely owns, are purged now; the caller leaves every other workspace; its
profile, settings and assistant sessions go. The sign-in at the auth
service stays: signing in again starts a new, empty account.

Delete a shared workspace. Only its owner can, with its ETag and its
exact name in ``confirm_name``.

It disappears for every member at once: every route under it answers 404
``workspace_not_found``. Its owner can restore it until ``purge_after``,
30 days later; then it is purged from every store. A personal workspace
is 409 ``personal_workspace_locked``: it goes with the account. A name
that does not match is 409 ``confirmation_mismatch``; a stale ETag 412
``stale_workspace``.

Its PDFs come back at once and its pages through ``job``: the answer is

collections they trashed; an admin any (403 ``workspace_role_required``

Move the collection, everything below it and the PDFs there to the
Trash, as one trash root. It is restorable for 30 days.

The subtree disappears from every list, path, grant and assistant
context at once. Its pages move to the Trash through ``job``: the answer
is 202 while there are pages to move, 200 when there were none. When
the subtree changed since the preview, nothing moves and the answer is
409 ``preview_changed``. Repeating the request that consumed the ETag
answers the same trash again.

post.description:
Record the author's decision on single operations of a pending set.

Recording a decision applies nothing: the editor applies the operations
the author accepts as ordinary edits and saves them through ``PUT``. An
operation is decided once, so the record is its own idempotency: a
repeated decision returns the change set with ``duplicate: true``, and a
contradicting one is 409 ``change_set_conflict`` with ``operation_index``.
That is why this route takes neither ``If-Match`` nor ``Idempotency-Key``.

post.description: Reject a whole pending change set. Rejecting it again changes nothing.

post.description:
Copy the page into another workspace, as a job in the target.

The caller must be an editor of both workspaces; a target it is not a
member of is 404 ``workspace_not_found``, a target collection that is not
there 404 ``collection_not_found``. The copy gets the content (blocks,
sources, citation style, name, tags) and, with ``include_pdfs``, the PDFs
located on the page (``located``) or those and the PDFs of the
collections it uses (``located_and_granted``), each a new PDF of the
target located on the copy. History, review, chats and PDF grants are
never copied. A replay with the same ``Idempotency-Key`` answers with the
same job; the same key with another body is 409
``idempotency_key_reused``.

Invite an address with a role (``admin``, ``editor`` or ``viewer``).

The answer carries the invitation's ``token``: the API sends no email, so
the inviter shares a link that carries it. Accepting needs the invited
address among the accepting account's verified addresses. The invitation
lapses after seven days; a new invitation for the same address revokes
the pending one. A replay with the same ``Idempotency-Key`` and body
answers the same invitation and token. A personal workspace is 409
``personal_workspace_locked``. It needs an admin.

Revoke a pending invitation; its link stops working. Revoking it again
changes nothing. An accepted one is 409 ``invitation_not_pending``. It
needs an admin.

get.description: A job's status and progress.
The workspace's active members, owners first. Every member sees it.

delete.description:
Remove a member, or leave the workspace (your own user id).

Any member can leave. Removing someone else needs an admin, and an admin
cannot remove an owner (403 ``workspace_role_required``). The last owner
can neither leave nor be removed: 409 ``last_owner``. The member loses
access at their next request, a running assistant run of theirs at its
next tool call. What they wrote stays with the workspace; their chats stay
private to them until the workspace is purged.

patch.description:
Give a member the ``admin``, ``editor`` or ``viewer`` role.

It needs an admin. An admin cannot change an owner: 403
``workspace_role_required`` with ``required_role: "owner"``. The last
owner keeps the role: 409 ``last_owner`` (ownership moves only through a
transfer). The member's new role holds from their next request.

delete.description:
Withdraw the pending transfer (the owner) or decline it (the member it
names). Anyone else, or no transfer, is 404 ``transfer_not_found``.

post.description:
Ask a member to become the owner. Only the owner can. Nothing changes
until that member accepts; the request lapses after seven days, and a new
one replaces it. A personal workspace is 409
``personal_workspace_locked``.

Accept the transfer that names you: you become the owner, and the
owner who asked becomes an admin. No transfer for you is 404
``transfer_not_found``; owning the most workspaces one account can have
already is 409 ``workspace_limit``.

get.description:
One page of the PDFs of a scope, newest first.

``context`` is what a page's assistant may read: the page's own PDFs,
those of every collection it is granted and of every collection below,
and the workspace's Unfiled PDFs. ``next_cursor`` is bound to this
workspace, caller and filter.

post.description:

Run the extraction now and return the resulting state.

Without ``force`` a ready extraction is kept. ``force`` extracts again
and replaces the Markdown; a forced attempt that fails leaves the PDF

post.description:
Bring a PDF the author moved to the Trash back to its location, or to
Unfiled when that page or collection is gone. An editor restores the PDFs
they trashed; an admin any. A PDF that is not in the Trash is 409
``not_in_trash``; one that went with its page or a collection comes back
with that page or collection.

Move a PDF to the Trash. It keeps its location and its extraction and
is restorable for 30 days; until then it is in no list, search or
assistant context. Trashing it again answers the same.

Bring back a deleted workspace, with everything it held.

Only its owner can, until its ``purge_after``; anyone else, and a
workspace past it, gets 404 ``workspace_not_found``. A live workspace is
409 ``workspace_not_deleted``. Owning the most workspaces one account can
have already is 409 ``workspace_limit``.

get.description:
The workspace's trash roots, newest first.

Each carries its ``kind``, ``name``, ``original_path``, who trashed it
and when, ``purge_after``, and for a collection the ``counts`` it holds
(the ``expected_*`` of deleting it forever). ``next_cursor`` is bound to
this workspace and caller.

delete.description:
Delete one trash root forever, as a job.

A collection needs the four ``expected_*`` counts the Trash shows for it
(428 ``precondition_required`` without them); when it holds anything
else now, nothing is deleted and the answer is 409 ``preview_changed``.
A page's PDFs are not deleted with it: they move to Unfiled.
